newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end down, sentiment weak.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end down, sentiment weak.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended down across the board on Thursday on weak market sentiment with investors expecting contracts to fall shortly, traders said.
The most actively traded July 1997 contract ended at 3,160 yuan ($381) per tonne, losing 15 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 3,170 and hit a low of 3,165 yuan per tonne.
September fell 18 to 3,170, November six to 3,145, the January 1998 contract 10 to 3,150 and March 10 to 3,070.
Combined volume fell to 19,500 tonnes from 16,100 tonnes.
Soybeans opened slightly lower and moved around the opening level for most of the session, traders said.
"Weak market sentiment was responsible for today's fall with many investors believing soybean futures having downward potentials in the next few days," one trader said.
"Another reason was that investors did not want to take physical delivery in the summer season," he added.
Traders said they expected soybeans to continue to fall in the short term.
